$comment: Vendoring contract for packages/engines. Checked by tools/check-vendored-engines.mjs; see that file for the model. The check is against the PINNED commit below and its committed manifest, never against engines HEAD: a guard pointed at HEAD goes red the moment canonical moves and then blocks every unrelated Suite PR. Moving the pin is a deliberate, reviewed vendoring pass. The Suite vendors the WHOLE canonical tree, so the expected state of this file is the one it is in: an EMPTY knownDeviations list. Any deviation that is genuinely deliberate goes in that list with a reason, a group and a burnDownWhen, and every differing or extra path is pinned to the blob currently vendored, so a second drift on an already-known path still fails. burnDownWhen states the condition under which the row must be removed, because a bare reason goes stale on its own: in NextGen a row reading "pull only with the recut in the same deploy window" became false the moment the recut merged and nothing in the file said so. A ledger entry whose deviation has gone is also a failure, so the list can only shrink.

vendoring.method: file-by-file reconciliation against a canonical clone, verified by blob hash with this guard, hashed from the files on disk rather than from the git index
vendoring.$comment: NOT a whole-tree `git subtree pull`. That silently DELETED 24 Suite-only downstream files on 2026-09-14. Vendor the paths the canonical range actually touched, then run the guard, which is what proves nothing else moved.
vendoring.lastVendoredRange: 3bac13cd88f4c38bd5c2a8e699b3b51349e65ead..8b8fb6a03814353f104c3bef70bb2efc1fe99bc9 (engines PR #201, the FC7-0 produced water repairs), on top of the FC5-0 relief pass that moved the pin to 3bac13c one merge earlier. FIVE canonical paths, four changed and one new, and the import closure needs nothing at all: engines/facilities/producedWater.js imports nothing. This one fixes four live wrong answers rather than only golden fields, all on the Produced Water Treatment Studio's own shipped defaults: a hydrocyclone whose unbounded centrifugal field made every liner REMOVED from the bank improve the reported water (the shipped 20 liners ran at 7.667 times design flow at 58,786 g and a cleared box gave one liner at 23,514,452 g), four device functions that returned a NaN cut size with no error key so the train skipped a stage and still printed MEETS with a 27.78 ppm margin, a flotation model whose attachment term was inert so induced and dissolved gas flotation were the same device, and a media filter that computed its removal twice by two routes that disagreed. BREAKING for callers: waterDensityKgM3 and oilDensityKgM3 now return { rhoKgM3 } or { error }; the only consumer is src/contexts/ProducedWaterContext.jsx, repaired in the same pull request. Blast radius in docs/scope/ProducedWater-STATUS.md.

testing.$comment: The Suite needs no equivalent of NextGen's tools/run-vendored-engine-tests.mjs. jest.config.js uses testMatch '**/__tests__/**/*.test.(js|jsx|ts)' with no testPathIgnorePatterns, so all 179 suites under packages/engines/__tests__ already run in `npm test` beside the Suite's own. There is no allow-list of known engine test failures because there are none: the vendored suites are green.
